   "source": [
    "# How to calculate the PDF and Intensity of from an XYZ file?\n",
    "\n",
    "First let's start off by importing the necessary libraries and loading the data."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import os\n",
    "import sys\n",
    "\n",
    "sys.path.insert(0, \"../../modules/\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from PyAESDebye import DebyeCalculator, readXYZ\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "# Read the xyz file\n",
    "positions = readXYZ(\"test.xyz\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The `readXYZ` function loads the data from the XYZ file. It calculates the box size based on the maximum and minimum values of the coordinates. This box size can be accessed using the `boxSize` attribute of the `positions` object. \n",
    "\n",
    "Now that we have the data loaded, we can create a calculator and calculate the PDF and Intensity. \n",
    "\n",
    "The calculator creation creates the cell pairs that can be used for the PDF calculations, this can be very quick for `nCells` < 15. For larger values of `nCells` the calculation can take upto a few seconds. You can refer to the documentation for more details no the arguments for the `DebyeCalculator` class.\n",
    "\n",
    "For the calculation to be run on a GPU, you can set the `useGPU` argument to `True`. This can be very useful for large systems, on consumer hardware where the CPUs are not quite as powerful and dont have a large number of threads."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "> ParallelHelper: worldSize: 1 world_rank: 0 omp_threads: 4 totalThreads: 4\n",
      "> Debye calculator initialized\n",
      "> CellList initialized with 10 cells\n",
      "> Setting up cell pairs ...complete! Took 0.0102749 s\n",
      "> Calculating PDF: I(4000 atoms) x J(4000 atoms)\n",
      "> PDF calculation complete!\n",
      "PDF calculation time:  0.1095731258392334 s\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "calculator = DebyeCalculator(nThreads=4, nCells=10, useGPU=False)\n",
    "\n",
    "pdf, pdf_time, pdf_test = calculator.calculatePDF(positionsI=positions)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"PDF calculation time: \", pdf_time, \"s\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "That's it! the PDF calculation is done. You can now calculate the intensity as follows:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "q_vector, intensity_vector, intensity_test = calculator.calculateIntensity(qStart=0, qEnd=10, nqSteps=1000, pdf=pdf)\n",
    "\n",
    "# plot the intensity\n",
    "plt.plot(q_vector, intensity_vector, label=\"Intensity\")\n",
    "plt.xlabel(\"q (1/Angstrom)\")\n",
    "plt.ylabel(\"Intensity\")\n",
    "plt.yscale(\"log\")\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
